prose.summary: Reconciled source purposes: [1] Define Universal Modules as reusable substrate-level semantic modules that own irreducible cross-domain primitives and are composed by higher-level domains rather than duplicated inside them. [2] Define the semantic surface a Universal Module may expose: schemas, relations, operations, events, roles and constraints intended for reuse across multiple Domains.

semantics.composition_rule: Domains compose Universal Modules by explicit refs/relations.
semantics.directory_rule: Universal Modules are represented under universal_module rather than legacy domains/json organization.
semantics.duplication_rule: Domain contracts reference substrate semantics instead of copying them.
semantics.extension_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] New Universal Module requires irreducible reusable semantics, not merely a convenient grouping. [2] Domain-specific semantics are not pushed back into substrate unless they are genuinely reusable cross-domain semantics.
semantics.identity_rule: Each Universal Module has independent stable canonical identity.
semantics.ownership_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] A Universal Module owns only its irreducible reusable semantics. [2] Each exposed semantic element has an explicit owning Universal Module or referenced external owner.
semantics.relation_rule: Substrate-local relations are explicit canonical relations.
semantics.reuse_rule: Same substrate identity may participate in any number of Domains.
semantics.trace_rule: Every Domain-resolved substrate element traces back to its Universal Module owner.
